newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends stronger on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends stronger on inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso was boosted on Monday from some $65 million worth of investment inflows and ended at 26.340 against the dollar from 26.343, traders said.
Dealers said they believed the inflows were for an investment in National Steel Corp.
As expected, the Central Bank limited the peso's strength through the purchases of $100 million at 26.337 and 26.339.
Volume rose to $207 million from $165.60 million.
"The Central Bank was there so there wasn't a sudden appreciation of the peso," a big bank trader said.
Banks have also been ligthening up on their dollar positions in anticipation of inflows from the proceeds of overseas borrowings, traders said.
They cited plans by Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co to launch $500 million worth of global bonds. Land Bank of the Philippines will also sell $200 million of five-year notes.
Traders said the peso would remain strong on Tuesday since oil firms have not posted their dollar requirements.
